findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics when input contains non-numeric text, empty lines, or out-of-range values
findings.failure_mode: untrusted external input causes process abort instead of returning a typed error; this is a panic path in production-reachable code
findings.fix: replace unwrap with proper error handling: change return type to Result<Vec<u32>, ParseError> and use ? or map_err to convert parse errors

findings.problem: unwrap() in production code is a panic path; parse() returns Result and ignoring it with unwrap violates panic-free standard
findings.failure_mode: any malformed line causes immediate process termination; no graceful error propagation
findings.fix: use Result<Vec<u32>, E> where E is a typed error, or collect valid results with Vec<u32> and track failures separately

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() returns Result which is silently discarded via unwrap; caller has no way to distinguish valid from invalid input
findings.failure_mode: fallible result is ignored; errors are converted to panic instead of being returned to caller for handling
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<u32>, Box<dyn Error>> or a custom ParseError enum so callers can handle failures explicitly

findings.problem: input.lines() iterates over all lines with no declared maximum bound; untrusted input could be gigabytes
findings.failure_mode: no static upper bound on iterations; unbounded iterator over untrusted input violates Rule 2 requirement for static termination proof
findings.fix: declare a maximum line count constant and validate input size before iteration, or use an explicit bounded take() iterator

findings.problem: collect::<Vec<u32>>() allocates a Vec without declared allocation budget; no with_capacity hint, no try_reserve for untrusted input growth
findings.failure_mode: untrusted input size leads to uncontrolled heap allocation; no graceful degradation when memory is exhausted
findings.fix: use Vec::with_capacity for known-bounded input, or declare max_size and call try_reserve before collection

findings.problem: no rust-toolchain.toml file; floating nightly is not acceptable for Holzman Rust work
findings.failure_mode: toolchain version is not pinned, reproducible builds cannot be verified
findings.fix: create rust-toolchain.toml with pinned nightly-YYYY-MM-DD, minimal profile, rustfmt, clippy, rust-src, llvm-tools-preview

findings.problem: function accepts &str and produces Vec<u32> with no stated allocation budget; parse_scores could be a hot path but has no allocation story
findings.failure_mode: no evidence of allocation counting or budget tracking; Vec growth behavior under various inputs is uncharacterized
findings.fix: state max expected lines and bytes; use with_capacity or arena if this is performance-critical; add allocation tracking if this is a hot path
